title: Trezor Model One officially launched
description: Trezor officially launched the Model One, the first production device in its hardware-wallet lineage.

title: Trezor Model T released
description: Trezor released the Model T, adding a touchscreen to the product line.

title: Physical read-protection downgrade attack disclosed
description: Kraken Security Labs disclosed a voltage-glitching attack that could extract seeds from Trezor Model One and Model T after physical access to the device.
notes: The disclosure described a hardware/microcontroller limitation rather than a remote compromise.

title: Trezor Suite officially launched
description: Trezor officially launched Trezor Suite as its desktop and web interface for Trezor hardware wallets.

title: Third-party support portal accessed without authorization
description: Trezor reported unauthorized access to a third-party support portal, potentially exposing names or nicknames and email addresses of users who had interacted with support.
affected_users_text: Up to approximately 66,000 users potentially affected
notes: Trezor stated that the incident did not threaten users' digital assets.

title: Trezor Safe 3 launched
description: Trezor launched Safe 3, introducing the Safe family and the first dedicated secure element in a Trezor device.

title: Trezor Safe 5 released
description: Trezor released Safe 5 as a premium touchscreen member of the Safe family.

title: Trezor Safe 7 launched
description: Trezor launched Safe 7, its first wireless Trezor generation with Bluetooth and magnetic wireless charging.

title: Model One and Model T e-shop sales ended
description: Trezor ended direct e-shop sales of Model One and Model T while committing to continued maintenance and critical security updates.
notes: This is end-of-sale, not end-of-support.

title: Shipping provider customer data breach disclosed
description: Trezor disclosed that ShipMonk, a third-party fulfillment partner, experienced unauthorized access exposing customer order information.
affected_users_text: Approximately 13,689 customers total; 11,742 with full exposure and 1,947 with partial exposure
notes: Trezor stated that its systems, products and services were not compromised. ShipMonk notified Trezor on 2026-08-10; investigation remained ongoing at disclosure.

title: Ledger Nano S launched
description: Ledger launched the Nano S hardware signer in 2016.

title: E-commerce and marketing database breach discovered
description: Ledger discovered unauthorized access to its e-commerce and marketing database through a third-party API key; later publication of the stolen database exposed a much larger set of customer records.
affected_users_text: More than 1 million email addresses and approximately 272,000 detailed customer records were later confirmed in the public dump.
notes: Ledger stated the breach did not compromise Ledger hardware wallets, the companion application, or customer funds.

title: Ledger Nano S Plus became generally available
description: Ledger made the Nano S Plus generally available.

title: Ledger announced Nano S retirement from production
description: Ledger announced retirement of Nano S production and replacement by Nano S Plus while stating existing Nano S support and maintenance would continue.

title: Malicious Ledger Connect Kit versions published through compromised NPM account
description: A former employee phishing compromise enabled malicious Ledger Connect Kit packages to be published to NPM and dynamically loaded by some dApps, causing a small number of users to sign draining transactions.
notes: Ledger stated the attacker did not gain access to Ledger infrastructure, source repositories, or the affected dApps themselves.

title: Ledger Stax shipping began
description: Ledger began shipping Ledger Stax to pre-order customers.

title: Ledger Nano Gen5 launched
description: Ledger launched Nano Gen5 at Ledger Op3n 2025.

title: Ledger Live renamed Ledger Wallet
description: Ledger transitioned the companion application branding from Ledger Live to Ledger Wallet.

title: Seed-generation entropy defect disclosed
description: COLDCARD disclosed a seed-generation defect in affected firmware lines. Fixed releases restore the intended hardware-randomness path for future seed generation, but existing affected seeds require migration unless an advisory exception applies.
notes: A firmware update fixes future seed generation but does not repair a seed that was already generated on affected firmware.

title: Fixed COLDCARD firmware released across supported model lines
description: Coinkite released fixed firmware for the supported COLDCARD model and track matrix and published migration guidance for existing affected seeds.

title: First MetaMask version shipped
description: MetaMask shipped its first public browser-wallet version.

title: MetaMask Mobile released on iOS and Android
description: Consensys announced the general release of MetaMask Mobile on iOS and Android.

title: Gnosis Safe smart account introduced
description: Gnosis Safe was introduced in 2018 as a general-purpose smart account.

title: Retail-focused Gnosis Safe mobile wallet discontinued
description: Safe later described the 2018 retail-focused mobile wallet as discontinued because of minimal adoption.
notes: The source establishes the lifecycle but not a precise discontinuation date; 2019 is an approximate ordering anchor.

title: Gnosis Safe rebranded to Safe
description: The project rebranded from Gnosis Safe to Safe after spinning out from GnosisDAO; Safe states that the protocol, audited contracts, accounts, funds, and security model did not change.

title: Bitkey began shipping
description: Bitkey exited pre-order status and began shipping its integrated hardware-and-mobile self-custody system.

title: Second-generation Bitkey introduced
description: Bitkey introduced a new hardware generation with an on-device screen while retaining the 2-of-3 multisignature system.

title: Relationship-enrollment randomness bug disclosed
description: Bitkey disclosed that the mobile app used a non-cryptographic random-number generator for a one-time relationship-enrollment secret. The demonstrated practical path was limited to narrow second-generation recovery-contact or inheritance flows and did not weaken wallet spending keys.
notes: Bitkey reported no evidence that customers were exploited or that funds were impacted; selected second-generation inheritance users were advised to update the app and re-enroll beneficiaries.

title: BitBox01 came to market
description: The first BitBox01 hardware wallet, later also known as Digital Bitbox, came to market.

title: BitBox02 launched
description: BitBox launched the BitBox02 Multi and Bitcoin-only editions; both editions use the same hardware with different firmware scope.

title: BitBox01 end-of-sale and end-of-life announced
description: Shift Cryptosecurity announced the BitBox01 end-of-sale and EOL process and encouraged migration to BitBox02.

title: BitBox01 entered end-of-life
description: BitBox later described the BitBox01 as end-of-life, meaning it no longer received updates while some functionality could continue temporarily.
notes: Year-level lifecycle anchor; later 2023 guidance confirms the device had been EOL for multiple years.

title: BitBox02 Nova introduced
description: BitBox introduced its next-generation BitBox02 Nova and opened pre-orders, with the original BitBox02 remaining in the lineup.

title: Two BitBox02 Nova firmware security issues disclosed and fixed
description: BitBox disclosed two physical-access firmware issues in BitBox02 Nova. The more relevant scenario could reveal a reused device password after an advanced attack, while the attacked device's seed remained protected.
notes: Original BitBox02 was explicitly not affected; BitBox reported no lost funds or evidence of exploitation.

title: Original Blockstream Jade launched
description: Blockstream launched its open-source Jade hardware wallet for Bitcoin and Liquid assets.

title: Blockstream Jade Plus launched
description: Blockstream launched Jade Plus while keeping the original Jade on sale and supported.

title: Jade RPC stack-overwrite vulnerability disclosed
description: Blockstream disclosed a descriptor-RPC memory-safety issue affecting Jade firmware 1.0.24 through 1.0.36 across Original Jade, Jade 1.1 and Jade Plus device types.
notes: Blockstream reported no evidence of exploitation in the wild and no confirmed loss of user funds.

title: Blockstream Jade Core introduced
description: Blockstream launched Jade Core as a streamlined additional hardware-wallet model.

title: Trust Wallet founded and mobile wallet launched
description: Trust Wallet began in 2017 as a mobile wallet before expanding to additional products.

title: Malicious Trust Wallet Browser Extension v2.68 published
description: An unauthorized malicious Browser Extension v2.68 was published to the Chrome Web Store using a leaked publishing API key, enabling theft from users who logged in during the affected period.
affected_users_text: 2,520 affected wallet addresses identified by Trust Wallet as of the July 17, 2026 update
notes: Trust Wallet stated the mobile app was not affected; investigation linked the incident to exposed developer secrets and Chrome Web Store API access.

title: Electrum created
description: Thomas Voegtlin created Electrum in 2011; the project has remained in continuous development as a lightweight Bitcoin wallet.

title: Argent rebranded to Ready
description: The wallet organization rebranded from Argent to Ready, retaining the lineage while clarifying distinct Ready product directions.

title: Ready announced migration of its mobile app from Starknet to Base
description: Ready announced that the Ready mobile app would move from Starknet to Base in mid-August 2026, while Ready X would continue supporting Starknet.
notes: Users with Starknet assets were advised to move or recover them through Ready X or another wallet before the app transition; assets remained self-custodial.

title: Zengo consumer MPC wallet launched
description: Zengo launched its consumer-facing wallet in 2019 using MPC/threshold signing rather than a traditional seed phrase model.

title: Tangem card-shaped wallet launched
description: Tangem states that its card-shaped Tangem Wallet was introduced in late 2021.

title: Phantom launched its iOS app
description: Phantom announced the general launch of its iOS mobile wallet application.

title: Phantom launched on Android
description: Phantom released its mobile wallet for Android after the earlier iOS launch.

title: Phantom disclosed remediation of the Demonic browser-extension vulnerability
description: Phantom disclosed a critical browser-extension vulnerability reported by Halborn in September 2021 and stated that fixes began rolling out in January 2022, with Phantom users protected by April 2022.
notes: The first-party disclosure characterizes the vulnerability as critical; this record does not infer confirmed Phantom-user theft from the disclosure.

title: Exodus Mobile Web3 browser became unavailable to newly created wallets
description: Exodus made the in-app Web3 browser unavailable for Exodus Mobile wallets created after April 22, 2026 while retaining the feature for eligible older wallets.
notes: This affects a feature inside Exodus Mobile and does not mean the separate Exodus Web3 Wallet browser extension was discontinued.

title: First-generation Passport introduced
description: Foundation states that its first-generation Passport hardware wallet, later described as the Passport Founder’s Edition, was introduced in mid-2020.

title: Second-generation Passport renamed Passport Core
description: Foundation renamed its existing second-generation Passport, previously referred to as Passport Batch 2, to Passport Core while keeping it in the product line alongside Passport Prime.
notes: This is modeled as a product rebrand, not a new hardware generation.

title: Xverse desktop browser extension launched
description: Xverse launched its desktop browser extension in beta for Chrome, adding a desktop wallet product alongside the existing mobile wallet.

title: Xverse Extension local seed-phrase logging issue disclosed
description: Xverse disclosed that browser behavior could cause a seed phrase to be written unencrypted to a local Chrome log during extension onboarding under certain conditions.
notes: Xverse stated the seed phrase never left the local device, mobile users were not affected, no exploits were reported, and no user funds were lost. Version 0.11.4 prevented new local logging; 0.11.5 additionally provided cleanup of previously cached logs.

title: Initial Sparrow Wallet release published
description: Sparrow's source history identifies August 29, 2020 as the initial public release of the desktop wallet.

title: Wasabi Wallet 1.0 released
description: Wasabi Wallet 1.0 was released after the earlier 2018 beta period, establishing the public desktop-wallet lineage.

title: Wasabi Wallet 2.0 released
description: Wasabi released its 2.0 generation as a major redesign of the existing desktop-wallet lineage.

title: zkSNACKs CoinJoin coordinator shut down
description: The zkSNACKs-operated Wasabi CoinJoin coordinator stopped operating on June 1, 2024. The open-source wallet remained active and current Wasabi clients can be configured to use other coordinators.
notes: This was a hosted coordinator-service shutdown, not discontinuation of the Wasabi Wallet software.

title: BlueWallet hosted lndhub.io Lightning service shut down
description: BlueWallet sunset its hosted lndhub.io Lightning service, ending new wallet creation and refill support before the May 31, 2023 shutdown while leaving regular Bitcoin wallets unaffected.
notes: BlueWallet continued to support self-hosted LndHub and its self-custody Bitcoin wallet; this event does not represent a BlueWallet shutdown.

title: Leather Wallet LLC acquired Hiro Wallet assets
description: Leather Wallet LLC, a Trust Machines subsidiary, announced that it had acquired the wallet assets from Hiro Systems PBC while preserving the wallet lineage.

title: Hiro Wallet rebranded to Leather
description: The existing Hiro Wallet desktop and browser-extension lineage was rebranded to Leather as the wallet became an independent brand under Leather Wallet LLC.

title: Browser-extension cached secret-key vulnerability reported
description: Leather's security history records a browser-extension issue where browser textarea caching could leave a private key or mnemonic in local storage under certain conditions, creating exposure if another party gained access to the computer.
notes: Leather records the report on August 8, 2023 and resolution on August 10, 2023 in extension version 6.3.1.

title: Leather Mobile launched
description: Leather launched its mobile wallet application for iOS and Android.

title: Leather Desktop deprecated
description: Leather deprecated its desktop wallet and stated that it would no longer receive updates or security fixes, directing users toward the browser extension.

title: MyCrypto brand launched
description: MyCrypto launched as a new Ethereum wallet-interface brand following the split between Taylor Monahan and the MyEtherWallet project.
notes: The February 10 launch FAQ describes the brand launch as having occurred within the preceding day; WLR retains month-level precision rather than inventing an exact launch timestamp.

title: MyCrypto Desktop officially launched
description: MyCrypto released its stable desktop applications and moved raw private-key, mnemonic, and keystore-file access out of the web interface into the desktop application.

title: Consensys acquired MyCrypto
description: Consensys announced the acquisition of MyCrypto to combine its work with MetaMask while MyCrypto stated that its existing products would continue operating in the short term.
notes: The acquisition announcement described gradual product convergence rather than an immediate MyCrypto shutdown.

title: Cobo Vault rebranded as Keystone
description: Keystone's official support documentation states that Cobo Vault was rebranded as Keystone on June 1, 2021 after the original hardware-wallet team left Cobo to create Keystone.
notes: The historical Cobo Vault hardware products are not yet canonical WLR products, so this entity-level continuity event intentionally has no affected_product_ids.

title: Keystone 3 Pro publicly introduced in official product design article
description: Keystone published its official Keystone 3 Pro product-design article as part of the 2023 Keystone 3 rollout chronology following the July forthcoming-launch announcement.
notes: This is an introduction/announcement anchor, not an asserted exact retail availability date.

title: Rabby browser-extension wallet introduced
description: The Rabby/DeBank team publicly introduced Rabby as a browser-extension wallet for DeFi users on July 26, 2021.

title: Rainbow Extension v1.2.39 added signature-security hardening
description: Rainbow Extension v1.2.39 deprecated support for dApps relying on the vulnerable eth_sign signing method and added sanitization of EIP-712 signature-request fields to mitigate common phishing attacks.
notes: This records a material security-hardening release, not a claim that a specific exploited Rainbow vulnerability existed.

title: Tangem Ring opened for public preorders
description: Tangem opened public preorders for the Tangem Ring on July 17, 2024 after unveiling the wearable hardware wallet at the 2023 Cardano Summit.
notes: This is a preorder milestone, not an asserted general-availability or shipping date. Tangem stated deliveries would begin later in 2024.

title: Tangem Mobile Wallet launched
description: Tangem introduced the Mobile Wallet as a free self-custody wallet available directly inside the Tangem app, with encrypted wallet keys stored in the smartphone security environment rather than a Tangem card or ring.

title: Exodus Web3 Wallet browser extension released
description: Exodus announced the release of its multi-chain browser extension, adding the Web3 Wallet product alongside its existing desktop and mobile applications.

title: External plugin authorization bypass disclosed
description: Electrum disclosed an external-plugin authorization bypass that could allow a rogue local process with filesystem write access to the Electrum data directory to execute arbitrary plugin code inside Electrum. The official advisory states the external-plugin system was affected from Electrum 4.6.0 until the fix in 4.7.2.
notes: Official Electrum GHSA-vw94-r84p-66qf. Private disclosure was received 2026-03-26; public disclosure occurred 2026-04-28. No exploitation or actual fund loss is inferred.

title: Nostr Wallet Connect spending-limit bypass disclosed
description: Electrum disclosed two flaws in its Nostr Wallet Connect plugin that could let a malicious or compromised NWC client spend above the configured daily limit through concurrent budget checks and millisatoshi truncation. The official advisory states the NWC plugin was affected from Electrum 4.6.0 until the fix in 4.7.2.
notes: Official Electrum GHSA-q7m2-785w-r585. Private disclosure was received 2026-03-02; public disclosure occurred 2026-04-28. Potential overspending is described by the advisory; no actual exploitation or loss is inferred.

title: Electrum 4.7.2 released with plugin security fixes
description: Electrum 4.7.2 was released with fixes for the external-plugin authorization bypass and the Nostr Wallet Connect daily spending-limit bypass later documented in the project security advisories.
notes: Both first-party Electrum security advisories state that version 4.7.2 was released on 2026-04-02 with the fixes included.

title: BitForge Lindell17 key-exfiltration vulnerability disclosed
description: Fireblocks publicly disclosed a Lindell17 implementation vulnerability initially discovered in Zengo that could leak key material across repeated failed signing attempts when an attacker had privileged access. Fireblocks and Zengo state that Zengo mitigated the issue through responsible disclosure and that no Zengo wallets were exploited.
notes: The public sources do not establish a Zengo app version range or an exact private remediation date, so WLR does not invent either. Fireblocks describes privileged access and repeated signing attempts as preconditions for the demonstrated attack.

title: Zengo publicly confirmed BitForge issue was addressed
description: Zengo published its response to the BitForge disclosure, stating that its research team worked with Fireblocks and promptly addressed the identified issue and that no Zengo users were impacted. Fireblocks separately confirmed Zengo had mitigated the Lindell17 issue.
notes: This event records the public remediation confirmation date, not an inferred patch-release date. No Zengo app version or exact private mitigation timestamp is asserted.

title: Rainbow Extension v1.1.0 added Demonic mitigation
description: Rainbow Extension v1.1.0 redesigned the secret-recovery-phrase import flow to mitigate the known Demonic browser-wallet vulnerability reported by Halborn.
notes: The official Rainbow release establishes that v1.1.0 contained the mitigation. WLR does not infer an affected-version range, exploitation, realized loss, Rainbow-specific severity, or the extension launch date from this source.

title: Rabby Swap smart contract exploited
description: Rabby reported that the Rabby Swap smart contract suffered a hack attack and that stolen funds were being tracked. Users who had used Swap were instructed to revoke existing approvals across chains, while Rabby stated that users who had not used Swap were unaffected.
affected_users_text: Users who had used Rabby Swap and retained approvals to the exploited contracts; Rabby stated that users who had not used Swap were unaffected.
notes: This is modeled as a feature-level smart-contract exploit affecting the then-current Rabby Browser Extension product, not as a browser key-storage compromise. WLR does not canonicalize an exact loss amount, affected-version range, or impact to later Mobile/Desktop products from these sources.

title: BlueWallet v7.0.9 fixed preferred Electrum server persistence
description: BlueWallet v7.0.9 fixed the preferred Electrum server persistence issue tracked as #7532, where a saved custom preferred server could be replaced by a suggested server after app restarts on the documented iOS reproductions.
notes: This is recorded as a software fix, not a vulnerability or exploit. WLR scopes the event only to BlueWallet Mobile because the reviewed reproductions are iOS/mobile; Desktop impact, server compromise, an affected pre-fix version range, and fund loss are not inferred.

title: Password-removal crash window could leave Sparrow wallet database unreadable
description: A Sparrow Wallet issue documented a narrow crash window during removal of a wallet password where the H2 wallet file could become unencrypted while seed or keystore state remained encrypted, causing Sparrow to reject the resulting inconsistent wallet database. Maintainer Craig Raw later said the race window appeared real but very small.
notes: WLR records this as a software issue rather than a CVE or exploit. The reviewed sources describe a reproducible but very narrow local crash/interruption window. The wallet file can become unreadable; retained seed material permits recovery, while a corrupted wallet file that is the only remaining seed-material copy can create a serious loss-of-access scenario. Maintainer Craig Raw characterized practical risk as mostly theoretical because the race window appeared to be only single-digit milliseconds under normal load. No confirmed fund loss is established, but the sources do not support a no-funds-affected claim, so funds_affected remains unknown. No general affected-version range is inferred.

title: Sparrow 2.4.2 released with password-removal database corruption fix
description: Sparrow 2.4.2 included the fix for possible database corruption during password removal, reordering database row and wallet-file encryption changes so a crash between the operations leaves the wallet in a recoverable state.
notes: The underlying mitigation commit was authored on 2026-03-06. WLR uses the 2026-03-10 public 2.4.2 release date for the remediation event and does not infer a broader affected-version range.

title: Ledger Live launched as Ledger companion application
description: Ledger launched Ledger Live as a new all-in-one companion application for Ledger devices on Windows, Mac, and Linux. The same product lineage was later renamed Ledger Wallet in 2025.
notes: This launch event belongs to the existing Ledger Wallet product lineage, which retains Ledger Live as a historical alias. The later 2025 rebrand event remains separate.

title: Trust Wallet Browser Extension launched for desktop browsers
description: Trust Wallet announced the launch of its new browser extension wallet on 2022-11-14, with availability for Chrome, Brave, and Opera at launch and support for EVM chains and Solana.
notes: This event is scoped to the Browser Extension product and does not alter the separate Trust Wallet Mobile product lineage. WLR does not infer launch-day support for browsers not named in the launch statement.

title: BitBoxApp launched as BitBox companion application
description: BitBox states that the BitBoxApp was launched in 2018 as the companion application for its hardware-wallet ecosystem. The reviewed first-party retrospective establishes the launch year but not a month or day.
notes: WLR records year precision only. This event describes the BitBoxApp product lineage and does not alter hardware-product launch dates or the later Android general-release timeline.

title: Hiro Wallet browser extension became available in Chrome and Firefox stores
description: Hiro announced general store availability of its wallet browser extension on 2021-08-10 for Chrome and Firefox. This browser-extension lineage was later acquired and rebranded to Leather in 2023.
notes: This launch event belongs to the current Leather Browser Extension lineage under its historical Hiro Wallet branding. Chrome/Firefox are historical launch-time distribution facts and do not replace the current-platform list.

title: Argent X launched on the Chrome Store for StarkNet
description: Argent launched Argent X on 2021-12-08 as a Chrome browser-extension wallet for StarkNet. The launch article explicitly distinguished Argent X from Argent’s separate mobile wallet. This product lineage later continued under the Ready X name.
notes: This event is scoped only to the current Ready X / historical Argent X product lineage. Chrome Store availability is the launch-time distribution fact established by the source; later Ready X platforms are not backdated to launch day.

title: Customer order data exposure disclosed
description: SafePal disclosed exposure of customer order information affecting approximately 40,000 customers. SafePal stated that private keys and seed phrases were not compromised.
notes: This is a customer/order-data privacy incident, not a wallet private-key, seed-phrase, or key-storage compromise. WLR does not infer compromise of wallet software, hardware, or signing keys from this disclosure.

title: Second-generation Passport launched as Passport Batch 2
description: Foundation later stated that it launched its second-generation Passport device in March 2022. This second-generation product was originally known as Passport Batch 2 and was renamed Passport Core in 2025.
notes: WLR records month precision only. The contemporaneous March 10, 2022 Batch 2 announcement was still at the presale stage, so that announcement date is not treated as an exact shipment or general-availability day.

title: SafePal S1 opened for sale
description: SafePal states that the S1 hardware wallet opened for sale on May 27, 2019, marking the commercial release of its first hardware wallet.
notes: The release date uses SafePal’s first-party progress update. Current SafePal history independently places the official S1 launch in May 2019.

title: SafePal Extension Wallet officially launched
description: SafePal announced the official launch of its browser extension wallet on August 19, 2022.
notes: The historical launch announcement listed Chrome, Firefox and Microsoft Edge. Current supported-browser status is governed separately by current distribution evidence and is not inferred from this 2022 event.

title: SafePal X1 Bluetooth hardware wallet officially launched
description: SafePal records the official launch and open-source release of its X1 Bluetooth hardware wallet in September 2023.
notes: Month-level precision is retained because the contemporaneous 2023-09-13 CEO letter announced the launch while still referencing preorder availability; no exact commercial-release day is inferred.

title: SafePal S1 Pro released through official channels
description: SafePal announced on September 7, 2023 that the S1 Pro was ready for distribution through official SafePal channels and available to order.
notes: The release date uses SafePal’s direct first-party S1 Pro release announcement rather than a later retrospective.

title: SafePal App added self-custody software-wallet capability
description: SafePal officially released SafePal Lite inside the SafePal App, allowing users to create or import self-custody software wallets in addition to using the App as a companion for SafePal hardware wallets.
notes: This event records the software-wallet capability release, not the initial SafePal App launch. First-party SafePal posts show that the App already existed in 2019.

title: COLDCARD Mk4 introduced
description: COLDCARD documentation records the Mk4 generation as introduced in 2022.
notes: Year-level precision is retained because the first-party documentation does not provide an exact release day in its launch statement.

title: COLDCARD Mk3 announced and first-batch preorders opened
description: Coinkite announced COLDCARD Mark 3, opened first-batch preorders, and stated that units were planned to ship by October 2019.
notes: This records the announcement and preorder opening only. It does not infer an exact commercial ship or release date.

title: COLDCARD Mk2 publicly described with new hardware and firmware changes
description: Coinkite publicly described the new COLDCARD Mk2, including mechanical buttons and hardware and firmware changes intended to harden the device against PIN-bypass attacks.
notes: This is a first-party public Mk2 disclosure milestone. It does not establish an exact commercial shipment or release date, so the product launch_date remains unresolved.

title: Safe Labs launched the rebuilt Safe Mobile app
description: Safe Labs launched a completely rebuilt Safe{Mobile} application for managing and signing Safe smart-account transactions on iOS and Android.
notes: This event tracks the current rebuilt Safe Mobile product and does not rewrite the separate lifecycle of the discontinued 2018 Gnosis Safe Mobile legacy app.

title: Keystone publicly detailed the Keystone 3 Pro
description: Keystone published a first-party product article detailing the Keystone 3 Pro hardware wallet and its community-driven design and security architecture.
notes: This is a first-party public product-announcement milestone. It does not establish the exact first commercial shipment or general-release day, so the product launch_date remains unresolved.

title: Exodus Mobile released
description: Exodus released the mobile version of its self-custody wallet platform in 2019 for iOS and Android.
notes: Year precision only; the reviewed first-party filing does not establish an exact first release day.

title: Argent mobile wallet launched on Ethereum
description: Argent launched its consumer smart-wallet product on Ethereum in 2018. This mobile product lineage later continued as Ready Mobile after the 2025 Argent-to-Ready rebrand.
notes: Year precision only. The first-party retrospective establishes the 2018 Ethereum launch but not a defensible month or day. Ready/Argent brand continuity is separately supported by existing canonical evidence wlr_src_000051.

title: Foundation Envoy released on mobile platforms
description: Foundation released Envoy during 2022 as a mobile Passport companion and Bitcoin software-wallet application for iOS and Android.
notes: Year precision only. Foundation stated on 2022-03-10 that Envoy would launch later, while the official Envoy repository published v1.0.7 Android/iOS release artifacts in October 2022 and Foundation subsequently described v1.0.7 as live on mobile platforms.

title: Rabby Desktop released in 2022
description: Rabby's official desktop source repository records desktop release packaging and a v0.1.1 release during 2022, establishing the desktop product as released by that year.
notes: Year precision only. The reviewed repository does not surface a v0.1.0 release commit, so WLR does not infer an exact initial launch day from the 2022-09-30 v0.1.1 commit.

title: BlueWallet Mobile released by 2018
description: BlueWallet's official source history records a store-versioned mobile build during 2018, establishing the mobile product as released by that year.
notes: Year precision only. The reviewed source history establishes a store/release lineage in 2018 but does not establish a defensible exact initial public-release day.

title: Keystone 3 Pro released in 2023
description: Keystone's first-party product history and official Keystone 3 firmware release lineage establish Keystone 3 Pro as a released product during 2023.
notes: Year precision only. A July 2023 Keystone article still described the launch as forthcoming, while Pro-specific first-party content and firmware release history appear later in 2023; no exact commercial launch day is inferred.

title: Rabby Mobile released in 2024
description: Rabby's official mobile repository establishes the transition from late-2023 development into a public mobile release lineage during 2024, including 0.1.0 publish preparation and an explicit 0.1.1 publish commit.
notes: Year precision only. The initial repository commit in 2023 is development evidence, not launch evidence; the 2024 publish-history does not establish one exact first public store-release day.

title: Rainbow Mobile released externally in 2019
description: Rainbow's official mobile-wallet repository records an external beta release in February 2019 and a v1.0.0 production release in June 2019, establishing the public mobile release lineage during 2019.
notes: Year precision only. Earlier 2018 beta-release commits do not clearly establish an external/public boundary; neither the 2019 external-beta commit nor the later production-release commit is treated as proof of one exact initial App Store launch day.

title: Rainbow Browser Extension released in 2023
description: Rainbow's official extension repository records a production release lineage in 2023, and Rainbow's public release-notes site independently confirms the extension's public release lineage during that year.
notes: Year precision only. 2022 Chrome Web Store manifest and publish-workflow preparation are not treated as launch evidence; neither the first reviewed Production version bump nor a later public release-note date is asserted as the exact initial store launch day.

title: SafePal App released in 2019
description: SafePal's first-party 2019 history establishes an active mobile-app release lineage, including an official App version announcement and a later statement that nine App versions had already been released.
notes: Year precision only. The July 2019 source concerns a DEX-capable official App version and already refers to the SafePal App; it is not treated as the exact initial App launch day. The May 2020 Software Wallet milestone is modeled as a later capability expansion rather than the initial App release.

title: BlueWallet Desktop released for macOS
description: BlueWallet announced that its first desktop product was out on the Mac Store on 2020-08-28.
notes: The first-party article directly states current Mac Store availability and identifies this as BlueWallet’s first desktop product, supporting day precision. No earlier source-code preparation is used to backdate launch.

title: COLDCARD Mk3 released in 2019
description: Coinkite's first-party production and retrospective sales history establishes that COLDCARD Mk3 entered the released/sold product lineage during 2019.
notes: Year precision only. The August 2019 announcement is explicitly preorder evidence and is not treated as launch; the reviewed sources do not establish one exact first shipping or sale day.

title: COLDCARD Mk2 released in 2019
description: Coinkite first-party product history and official firmware hardware support establish the mechanical-key COLDCARD Mk2 lineage during 2019.
notes: Year precision only. Late-2018 firmware still documents the older touch-key hardware lineage; January/February 2019 first-party history establishes the Mk2 hardware boundary without one exact first sale or shipping day.

title: Passport Prime began shipping in 2025
description: Foundation first-party shipping history establishes that Passport Prime entered its shipping/release lineage during 2025 after the 2024 announcement and preorder period.
notes: Year precision only. Foundation still described future Early Access shipping in May 2025 and later stated that Passport Prime was beginning to ship in October 2025; no exact first shipment day is asserted.

title: Xverse Mobile publicly available during 2021
description: Contemporaneous audit and mobile-store distribution evidence establish the Xverse Wallet mobile product during 2021.
notes: Year precision only. The reviewed evidence safely establishes public mobile availability during 2021 but does not justify one exact initial store-release day.

title: MetaMask Extension critical clickjacking vulnerability disclosed
description: MetaMask reported a critical Extension-only clickjacking vulnerability that could render the wallet UI as a hidden layer over a malicious site and trick users into revealing private data or sending crypto-assets. MetaMask awarded the reporting team a $120,000 bounty and stated that Extension 10.14.6 and later were protected.
notes: Month precision is intentional: the reviewed first-party source establishes a June 2022 disclosure but not one defensible exact public disclosure day. MetaMask reported no known exploitation before the patch, but WLR does not convert that into a stronger funds_affected=no claim.

title: Demonic vulnerability exposed MetaMask Extension recovery phrases on disk
description: Halborn disclosed CVE-2022-32969, known as Demonic, in which browser session-restore behavior could cache an imported Secret Recovery Phrase to disk in plaintext under specified conditions. MetaMask Extension versions before 10.11.3 were affected; MetaMask implemented mitigations in 10.11.3 and later, and MetaMask Mobile was not affected.
notes: Halborn's 2022-06-15 coordinated public disclosure supplies the event date. NVD rates CVE-2022-32969 at CVSS 3.1 5.9 MEDIUM and records MetaMask versions before 10.11.3 as affected. First-party MetaMask reporting explicitly excludes MetaMask Mobile. No confirmed funds-loss statement is established, so funds_affected remains unknown.

title: Safe{Wallet} Web supply-chain compromise enabled targeted Bybit transaction manipulation
description: A targeted compromise of a Safe{Wallet} developer workstation and Safe{Wallet} web-delivery infrastructure enabled malicious JavaScript to manipulate a Bybit Safe transaction on 2025-02-21. The manipulated transaction resulted in approximately $1.46 billion in assets leaving Bybit's affected Ethereum cold wallet.
amount_text: Approximately $1.46 billion from Bybit's affected Ethereum cold wallet
notes: The product boundary is Safe{Wallet} Web. Safe stated that external forensic review did not identify vulnerabilities in Safe smart contracts or in the source code of the frontend/services. Sygnia describes the incident as a supply-chain compromise and traces the attack path from a compromised Safe developer workstation through Safe AWS access to injected JavaScript served from app.safe.global. The malicious code was highly targeted to the Bybit Safe; this record does not generalize the impact to all Safe accounts or Safe Mobile.

title: Safe{Wallet} rebuilt infrastructure and rotated credentials after targeted compromise
description: Safe reported that the Safe{Wallet} team fully rebuilt and reconfigured infrastructure, rotated all credentials, eliminated the identified attack vector, and restored Safe{Wallet} on Ethereum mainnet with a phased rollout and additional security measures.
notes: This remediation is infrastructure- and credential-based, so WLR does not invent an affected-version or fixed-version range. The 2025-02-28 date is the public disclosure date of the completed rebuild/credential-rotation boundary, not an asserted exact completion timestamp for every remediation action.
